title: What's happening right now
goal: Tell habits apart from things happening right now, and use the رہا / رہی / رہے ہیں forms correctly.
bekal: building "-ing" sentences with root + رہا/رہی/رہے + ہوں/ہے/ہیں
telling میں کھاتا ہوں apart from میں کھا رہا ہوں
talking on the phone about what you are doing

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — فون پر
dialogs.intro: Hasan calls Budi in the late afternoon. It sounds noisy at both ends.

lines.text: اچھا! میں روز شام کو بازار جاتا ہوں، لیکن آج جلدی جا رہا ہوں۔

lines.literal: then soon back come-please. we you of waiting do staying are.

lines.literal: you my waiting why do staying are?

lines.baca: āj ammī biryānī banā rahī haiñ. āp ke liye!

lines.literal: today mom biryani make staying is. you of for!

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: واہ! میں ابھی آ رہا ہوں!

notes: **Compare Budi's two sentences side by side.** میں روز بازار جاتا ہوں = "I usually go to the market" (habit). میں ابھی بازار جا رہا ہوں = "I'm going to the market" (right now). The difference in form is tiny — one word, رہا, slipped in — but the difference in meaning is big, and Urdu speakers never mix them up.

**The word رہنا on its own means "to stay, to remain".** That's why the formula makes sense: کھا رہا ہوں is literally "eat, staying, am" — the action is still going on. English does something similar with "keep": "keep eating", "keep waiting".

**This form is also used for weather.** بارش ہو رہی ہے = "it's raining", literally "rain is happening". Notice رہی, because **بارش is feminine**. ہوا چل رہی ہے ("the wind is blowing") is feminine too. And برف پڑ رہی ہے ("it's snowing") uses the verb پڑنا, literally "snow is falling".

**"To wait" is انتظار کرنا, and it needs a special pattern.** "I'm waiting for you" is میں آپ کا انتظار کرتا ہوں — literally "I do your waiting". The person being waited for comes in as the **owner** of the waiting. It feels very odd at first, but after five uses it becomes automatic.
**The words امی and ابو take the respectful plural.** امی کھانا پکا رہی ہیں — notice ہیں, even though there is only one mother. The respect rule from unit 3 applies fully to every verb form.

**The word واپس means "back", and it pairs with verbs.** واپس آنا (come back), واپس جانا (go back), واپس دینا (give back). It isn't a verb on its own but a direction word — just like "back" in English.

grammars.title: The "-ing" form: root + رہا/رہی/رہے + ہوں/ہے/ہیں
body: The formula is exactly like the habitual form, except the ending ـتا/ـتی/ـتے is replaced by the word رہا/رہی/رہے, which stands **separately** after the root.
What decides رہا · رہی · or رہے is still **the gender and number of the subject** — the same rule as unit 7, so there's nothing new to memorize.
after: For the negative, put نہیں before the root, and unlike the habitual form, **ہوں/ہے/ہیں stays**: میں نہیں جا رہا ہوں ("I'm not going"). Dropping it makes the sentence sound broken.

grammars.title: When to use which
body: If you're unsure, ask yourself one question: **is this action going on right now?** If yes, use the "-ing" form. If it describes a habit, a fact, or a schedule, use the habitual form.

head: Situation

Meaning
rows: پاکستان میں بارش کم ہوتی ہے۔

after: ⚠️ Unlike English, the Urdu "-ing" form is **not** used for future plans. "I'm going to Karachi tomorrow" is not میں کل کراچی جا رہا ہوں but میں کل کراچی جاؤں گا — the future form, which comes in unit 14.

blocks.title: Talking about the weather — a safe conversation starter anywhere
items: Asking: آج موسم کیسا ہے؟ ("what's the weather like today?") · باہر گرمی ہے؟ ("is it hot outside?")
Answering: آج بہت گرمی ہے۔ ("it's very hot today") · بارش ہو رہی ہے۔ ("it's raining") · موسم بہت اچھا ہے۔ ("the weather is lovely")

Summer in Lahore runs from May to September and is truly tough — 45 degrees Celsius is nothing unusual. A sentence you'll hear every day: بہت گرمی ہے، ہے نا؟ ("so hot, isn't it?"). The tag ہے نا؟ means "right?" and attaches to the end of any sentence.

میں بازار جا رہا ہوں۔ — بارش ہو رہی ہے۔ — بچے کھیل رہے ہیں۔ — ہم آپ کا انتظار کر رہے ہیں۔ — میں ابھی آ رہا ہوں۔
wave: Throughout one day, every time you switch activities, say to yourself میں … رہا/رہی ہوں. Ten times a day is enough to make it automatic.
